'''Guise''', officially the '''Republic of Guise''', is an country located at the very tip of the [[Salal peninsula]]. It borders [[Peka]] to the north, the [[Rianian Ocean]] to the south and west, and [[Uscea Sea]] to the north. [[Tosakaa]] is the largest city and capital. Guise is the second-least populous country in Atirha after Metndria, with about [[List of countries and dependencies by population|830,000 inhabitants]]. It spans an area of 8,590 square kilometres (3,320 sq mi), making it the second smallest country in Atirha after Tomscilus at. Culturally, Guise is considered very close to Emara.

The area of Guise was first colonised by the [[Taval|Tavalans]] in 1273. The colony was taken over by [[Lycroa]] around 1325 after the [[Aniqen disappearance]]. The [[Emara|Emaran]] colonisation of the area started in the late 14th century. Guise remained part of the [[Emaran Empire]] until it became a [[Emaran dominion|dominion]] in 1677; it gained [[independence]] in 1717. A [[1719 coup]] toppled the democratically elected government of [[Cars Deaa]] and began a long period of military influence. In 1725, Guise implemented a [[new constitution]], but mounting political unrest culminated in the [[1727 Guise coup d'état]] by Tiepoi. His autocratic government was overthrown in January 1731 by the [[Etirhan invasion]] during the [[Guisen Revolution]]. 

Revenue from the [[Cars Harbour]] has continued to represent a significant portion of Guise's GDP, especially after the [[Western Harbour expansion project]] (finished in 1762) doubled its capacity. Commerce, banking, and tourism are major sectors. Guise is regarded as having a [[wikipedia:World_Bank_high-income_economy|high-income economy]]. In 1765, Guise ranked [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|8th in the world]] in terms of the Krali Total Development Index. In 1764, Guise was ranked the [[seventh-most competitive economy]] in the world, according to the Global Economic Forum's Global Competitiveness Index. Guise was ranked [[22nd in the Global Innovation Index in 2025]]. Covering around 40 per cent of its land area, Guise's forests are home to an abundance of tropical plants and animals – some of them found nowhere else on Andah.
